title: Tenant-scoped deletion orchestration and verifiable purge playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers require a repeatable, tenant-scoped workflow that can (1) enforce retention policies across regions, (2) perform automated deletion for right-to-be-forgotten requests, and (3) produce cryptographically verifiable evidence bundles for audit and regulatory reporting. Current ad-hoc scripts and manual runbooks are slow to operate at scale and provide insufficient tamper-evident proof for audits. Goal: Deliver a playbook and orchestration primitives that enable customers and Redwood operators to run tenant-scoped purges that are fully auditable, provably completed, and can be replayed/verified by third-party tools. The solution should integrate with the retention engine, the private deployment control plane, and the Console evidence exporter. Key outcomes: automated purge orchestration, per-tenant proof bundles with signatures and manifests, webhook/attestation API for customers, and an optional dry-run mode for safe validation before irreversible deletes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Product exposes a tenant-scoped deletion flow in the Console (UI + API) that accepts retention policy or RTBF request ID and region scope.
A2: Orchestration engine can execute staged deletes with pre-checks, dry-run, and post-verification steps across multi-region stores without manual operator intervention.

A3: After completion, system emits a single 'purge evidence bundle' containing (a) deletion manifest, (b) cryptographic checksum set, (c) operation timeline, and (d) operator signature which can be downloaded from the Console and retrieved via API.
A4: Evidence bundle verifies on a reference verifier tool (internal) and test customers can validate bundle integrity using public attest keys exposed in the compliance API.
A5: Webhook/attestation API notifies customer systems of progress states (started, blocked, completed, failed) and includes an immutable reference to the evidence bundle.
A6: Rollback/compensating step is available during 'pre-commit' window in UI with audit trail; irreversible delete only proceeds after acceptance of post-checks or expiry of the window.
A7: End-to-end integration tests exist for: single-tenant RTBF, cross-tenant isolation check, and cross-region purge with verification; tests run in CI and are stable.
A8: Documentation and customer-facing playbook published in the Compliance section of the docs; includes sample API calls, expected evidence bundle format, and recommended retention settings.
A9: Security review completed and the implementation meets KMS signing requirements and least-privilege operator roles.
A10: Metrics emitted to the Console: purge duration, items deleted, verification failures, and evidence downloads; baseline dashboards created.
A11: Migration plan for customers with existing manual purge workflows documented in Confluence and linked from the Console guidance.
A12: Privacy team sign-off on language and customer notice templates used during RTBF workflows.
technical_notes: Orchestration model: orchestrator composes a directed sequence of idempotent steps: discovery -> lock -> dry-run -> staged-delete -> verify -> seal-evidence -> notify -> release-lock.
Evidence bundle: tar.gz containing JSON manifest, per-shard checksums, operator/public key signatures, and a canonicalized metadata file. Bundle format v1 documented in compliance spec link.
KV/cache considerations: ensure in-memory caches and KV caches are invalidated as part of staged-delete; add short-lived tombstones to avoid resurrection from replicas.
Cross-region: use region-aware connectors and ensure deletion tasks are retried with region affinity; include region stamp in manifest for legal residency proof.
Security: sign evidence bundle with KMS/HSM-backed key; include key rotation considerations and revocation metadata.
Observability: trace context propagated through orchestration steps; add per-tenant correlation ID and expose to Console timeline UI.
API contract: new endpoints: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/purges (start), GET /v1/purges/{id}/evidence (download), POST /v1/purges/{id}/verify (replay verification).
Dry-run mode: simulate deletes and produce a verification-only bundle flagged as non-authoritative (cannot be used as final attestation).
Operator roles: 'purge-operator' role required for manual confirmation; RBAC enforced in private/control plane and hosted with SSO mapping.
Backpressure and rate limits: orchestrator must respect quota/throughput constraints and provide safe throttling to avoid impacting tenant production traffic.
out_of_scope: Automated permanent deletion of third-party backups (separate backup lifecycle management).
Customer-managed offline archival workflows outside Redwood control plane.
Legal hold workflows (these will be handled in a follow-up project).
